summary: Joel Tatelman specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned his PhD from the University of Oxford by 1996 under the supervision of Alexis Sanderson and later taught Tamara Cohen.
Joerg Tuske works in philosophy and Indology. He held an attested post at the University of Cambridge in 1998 and served as Associate Professor of Philosophy at Salisbury University in 2013.

Joey Hung is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at PLK Fong Wong Kam Chuen Primary School, Po Leung Kuk Centenary Li Shiu Chung Memorial College, and the Hong Kong Academy for Performing Arts, later holding a post at Dharma Drum Buddhist College.
Jogendra Singh is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at Nava Nalanda Mahavihara under Uma Shankar Vyas.

Jogindra Nath Samaddar (1884–1929) worked in Indology and history and archaeology. Educated at Bangabasi College and Presidency College, Chennai, he held lectureships at Pramatha-Manmatha College, St. Columba's College, Patna College (1912), and Patna University (1923).

Johan Elverskog works on Iranian and Central Asian, Buddhist, and religious studies. Educated at UC Berkeley (BA ~1989–1993) and Indiana University (MA ~1993–1995), he was a fellow at UC Santa Barbara (1997–1998) and became a professor at Southern Methodist University (~2002).

Johan Hendrik Caspar Kern (1833–1917) was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at Utrecht and Leiden (PhD 1855) under Antonie Rutgers and in Berlin under Albrecht Weber. He taught at Varanasi (1863–1865) and held Leiden's Sanskrit chair (1865–1903).
Johan Hendrik Kern (1867–1933) was a linguist. He held academic posts at the University of Groningen from 1901 to 1924 and at Leiden University from 1924 to 1933.

Johan Huizinga (1872–1945) was a historian and Indologist. He studied at the University of Groningen (~1891–1895) and Leiden University (~1896–1897) under J. H. C. Kern, later holding posts at Groningen (1905–1915) and Leiden (1914–1942).

Johann Andreas Schmeller (1785–1852) attended the Wilhelmsgymnasium. He taught at the Real Instituto Militar Pestalozziano and Bavarian Cadet Corps, served as custodian at the Bavarian State Library (1829), and was a professor of Old German at the University of Munich (1828, 1846).
Johann Caspar von Orelli (1787–1849) was a linguist who taught at the Cantonal School of Graubünden (~1813–1819), the Carolinum Zürich (~1819–1833), and the University of Zurich (~1833–1849).

Johann Christoph Adelung (1732–1806) was a linguist who studied at Kloster Berge school and the University of Halle. He taught at Evangelisches Ratsgymnasium Erfurt (1758) and was head librarian at the Saxon State and University Library Dresden (1787).
Johann Elias Schlegel (1719–1749) was educated at Schulpforta (~1733–1739) and studied at the University of Leipzig (~1739–1742).

Johann Friedrich Blumenbach (1752–1840) studied at Ernestinum Gotha and the universities of Jena (~1769–1772) and Göttingen (~1772–1775). He held a post at the University of Göttingen from circa 1776 until 1840.

Johann Friedrich Herbart (1776–1841) was a philosopher who studied at the University of Jena (~1794–1797). He held a post at the University of Göttingen from circa 1802 to 1809 and taught Eduard Röer.

Johann Friedrich Pfaff (1765–1825) was educated at Karlsschule Stuttgart and the University of Göttingen (1785–1787). He held posts at the University of Helmstedt (1788–1810) and Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (1810–1825).

Johann Gildemeister (1812–1890) was an Indologist educated at Göttingen and Bonn under Heinrich Ewald, Georg Wilhelm Freytag, Christian Lassen, and A. W. von Schlegel. He held professorships at the University of Marburg (~1845–1859) and the University of Bonn (~1859–1890).

Johann Gottfried Eichhorn (1752–1827) was a scholar in religious studies, history, and linguistics. He studied at the University of Göttingen under C. G. Heyne and held professorships at the University of Jena (1775) and the University of Göttingen (1788).

Johann Gottfried Ludwig Kosegarten (1792–1860) was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at the University of Greifswald and under Silvestre de Sacy, later serving as professor at the University of Jena (1817–1824) and the University of Greifswald (1824–1850).

Johann Gottfried von Herder (1744–1803) was a philosopher and linguist. Educated at the University of Königsberg (1761), he held posts at Collegium Fridericianum, Riga Cathedral School, Wilhelm-Ernst-Gymnasium (1776–1803), and as General Superintendent for the Court of Saxe-Weimar-Eisenach (1776).
